chunks: Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed his mother, would he inherit her? He (peace be upon him) said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: Whichever man with a kinship bond kills his relative, he will not inherit from him.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.لَمْ يَرِثْهُ: He does not inherit from him

ai.seo_question: Does a killer inherit from the person they killed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'gharamah' (exclusion from inheritance) for the killer, specifically addressing the case of patricide/matricide. Abu Abdullah (AS) cites a general rule from his father that any relative who kills a close kin is barred from inheriting, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse 4:11 and elaborated upon in Shia jurisprudence as a divine penalty preventing the murderer from benefiting from the victim's wealth.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who killed his mother, would he inherit her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> heard my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever man with relationship kills his relative, would not inherit from him (the one who has been killed)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id has narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has killed his mother; if he can inherit her. He (the Imam) said, ‘I heard my father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, “Whoever of the relatives kills one of his relatives he cannot inherit from that relative.’””
